learning_objective: 🎯 Unleash your imagination! Learn how to craft engaging stories, articles, and descriptions using powerful vocabulary and vivid imagery.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Instead of writing 'He was angry' (Telling), write 'His face turned red and he slammed his fist on the table' (Showing). Paint a picture with your words.
Use the five senses (sight, sound, smell, touch, taste) to describe the environment. Make the reader feel like they are standing right inside your story.
A good story has a Beginning (introduces characters/setting), a Middle (a conflict or problem arises), a Climax (the peak action), and an Ending (resolution of the problem).
Enhance your writing using Similes (as brave as a lion), Metaphors (he has a heart of stone), and Personification (the wind whispered) to make the text beautiful and poetic.
Creative writing isn't just stories. Articles and speeches require a catchy title, a strong opening quote, real-world examples, and a powerful concluding thought to inspire the audience.

fun_activity.title: 🎨 The 5 Senses Challenge
fun_activity.instructions: Look at an apple. Write 5 sentences describing it without using the word 'apple'. One for how it looks, one for smell, one for touch, one for the sound of biting it, and one for taste!

exam_tips: 📌 When writing a story in the exam, always give it an interesting title. If a starting line is provided, you MUST begin your story with those exact words.
📌 Keep your character count low. In a short story, 2 or 3 characters are enough. Too many will make the plot confusing.
📌 For Article writing, use rhetorical questions (e.g., 'Have we forgotten our humanity?') to keep the reader engaged.
quick_recap: ⭐ Good creative writing makes the reader feel emotions (fear, joy, suspense).
⭐ The climax is the turning point of the story where the tension is at its absolute highest.
⭐ Always proofread your creative work; a great story is easily ruined by bad spelling and grammar.
